title: 1974: Lionel Hampton, jail and the Cotton Club band
summary: Howard recounts bailing Lionel Hampton out of Long Beach jail and bathing him for the matinee, and names players in the band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: What about the period -- you know, I guess you were part of that group when Lionel -- Lionel Hampton was working in Los Angeles years ago. Was
that on Main Street or someplace? If you can clear that up in my mind (Unintelligible) -- I've heard many stories.
Boy, you've got to start way back.
Okay.
Lionel never got up that far that fast.
I know, but wasn't he in Los Angeles --
Well, the first thing -- you may not want to use this -- the first thing I did I had to go get him out of jail in Long Beach and put him on the bandstand to play.
(Laughter)
Well, did you know him before that?
I guess you did because you got him out of jail.
(Laughter)
Yeah, I knew him. I don't like to talk like that.
Well, we can use as much as we want.
Well, at this period --
Well, if he was here I'd say it right in front of him.
Yeah.

I'd say, 'Don't get fresh now because I knew you when you didn't have nothing, didn't have a pot to piss in, and I'd get with you, too.' And I would, see. I'd get with him. I had to go get him out of bed. Get him out of bed, he'd be so drunk, and put him in the bathtub and bathe him and take him down to do the -- that matinee at Sebastian's Cotton Club.
Get him out of bed.
Was that when you had the band there at the Cotton Club?
Uh-huh.
Who were some of the other people who were there that we might know?
In the band?
Yeah.
Country Allen. George Orfendorff That's the two brass. Leon Herringford. He's gone.
Yeah. How about the drummer? Did Lionel play drums or vibes?
Lionel was playing drums then. See, Henry had gone, Henry Allen. You've heard of him? Tin Can we called him.
I've heard of Tin Can, yes.
(Laughter)
He was something else, too. He's gone.
